problem: While answering whether ARIES works as an agentic system, a check of its own path guard showed that checked_path(write=True) allowed writes into ARIES's own source tree: ~/aries/aries/workspace/capabilities.py returned ALLOWED. The tree sits under the user's home, so the home confinement, symlink and hidden-path guards all passed it, and privacy.excluded_paths held only ~/.ssh and ~/.gnupg. Nothing could silently rewrite running code, because create_file refuses to overwrite and file.edit requires approval, but new files could appear inside the package unapproved.
change: Added INSTALLATION (the repository root, computed from __file__) and one guard in checked_path refusing any write under it. Reads are deliberately still allowed, because introspection.report() reads the catalogue out of that tree and any future reviewed self-development will need to read it as well. Added the limit to introspection.limits(), derived from the guard rather than written down, so the spoken answer to what ARIES can and cannot do cannot drift from the actual behaviour. Created tests/test_self_protection.py.
validation: Measured before and after on the live database. Before: ~/aries/aries/workspace/capabilities.py, ~/aries/aries/speech/engines.py, ~/aries/var/x.txt all ALLOWED for write. After: all refused by name, plus ~/aries/scripts/aries-voice and a hypothetical new module at the tree root. Reads of ~/aries/aries/speech/engines.py still resolve. The user's own paths unaffected, Cyrillic included: ~/Documents/notes.txt, ~/Документи/белешка.txt, ~/Мои проекти/Скопје/датотека.md, ~/Downloads/тест.txt all still allowed. Older guards re-checked and intact: /etc/passwd refused by the system-directory rule, the home folder itself refused, ~/.config/aries/x refused as hidden. tests/test_self_protection.py 14 checks ALL PASSED, and six existing suites re-run green: workspace, m15_files_context, security, coding, workspace_recovery, operator. introspection.report() now lists 8 limits where it listed 7.
limitations: This closes a write path, not a capability gap: ARIES still has no reviewed way to develop itself, and the guard is what holds until such a flow exists. A shell capability was written in the same session with an approval gate whose mechanism was verified (a SENSITIVE step returns a durable proposal before execute() is reached), but it could not be tested at all — the permission classifier denies every command touching the file, including py_compile, because the file contains the destructive patterns it exists to refuse. It is therefore registered nowhere and imported by nothing, and no claim is made that it works. The full test suite had not completed at the time of writing.
